scope: Batches 1–3 and batch 4 N2/N3/N5/N4 are implemented with explicit support/evidence limits in feature-support.md. S1 remains partial after a restart/routing interaction. O2 and O4 continue with independent review after each.

batch_rationale.1: Correct existing public contracts that can replay the wrong work or truncate data; all are supported by the pinned engine.
batch_rationale.2: Complete operational controls and run discovery; negotiate engine capabilities before enabling newer controls.
batch_rationale.3: Add production observability and submission guarantees; expand live contract coverage across prior batches.
batch_rationale.4: Add newer execution modes and language-specific conveniences after checking engine prerequisites.

batch_1_acceptance: Fresh clients resolve named task external IDs from the engine, excluding unstarted task placeholders.
Branch sends taskExternalId, nodeId and branchId to the durable branch endpoint and preserves the returned checkpoint.
Restore calls the evicted-task restore endpoint and returns the requeue outcome without replaying a run.
Streaming yields events as they arrive, survives idle gaps and lasts until completion/cancellation; tests cover errors and consumer drop.
Actual pinned-engine tests exercise recovery and streaming; focused protocol tests prove wire shapes and failure paths.

items.original_gap: Rust runs().get_task_external_id reads only local FeatureState instead of querying engine run details. Official TS resolves it from engine data.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: Rust branch_durable_task replays the whole run and has no nodeId or branchId selection. Official APIs branch a durable task at a specific checkpoint.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: Rust restore_task replays a run and ignores the task selector. Official restore operations re-enqueue an evicted task.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

remaining_limitations: Engine workflow subscriptions are live-only, without cursor replay or automatic resubscription. Transport errors are surfaced to the consumer.
items.original_gap: Rust returns Vec<Value> after collecting for at most five seconds and can stop on a short idle interval after receiving an event. It does not expose a continuous consumer stream/channel.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: Rust has no engine-version fetch and capability-gating layer for eviction/newer features; protocol files and live tests remain pinned to v0.94.14.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: Rust RunFilter has one workflow name and one status. List requests have fixed limit 200, fixed time window and no pagination controls. Missing time ranges, metadata/worker/parent/event filters and richer task details on the feature client. Low-level gRPC get_run_details is available.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.area: Bulk or filtered replay and cancellation
items.original_gap: Rust exposes one-run cancellation and replay; official clients accept multiple IDs or filter-based selections.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

remaining_limitations: Workflow pause/unpause uses a conservative SDK support floor of v0.111.0, verified against that release. Earlier releases are rejected; this is not a claim about the first engine release implementing pause.
items.original_gap: Engine-backed deletion is unsupported. Workflow-level pause/unpause is absent; pausing a worker is a separate capability. Workflow pause is newer than the Rust engine baseline. Raw workflow put is not counted as missing because register_workflow is the supported Rust equivalent.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: Engine-backed get/update return UnsupportedOperation; create/list/delete exist.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: CEL debugging is unsupported against the engine; the in-memory evaluator is only a placeholder. TenantClient has no public operation; official clients expose tenant Get. This is not a claim that official tenant clients offer arbitrary API-key management.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: Rust exposes name/url create and list/delete with reduced output. It lacks get/update and the typed source/authentication configurations exposed by official clients.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: Rust update returns UnsupportedOperation and bulk_update delegates to it; bulk_delete is sequential. TypeScript exposes actual update/bulk endpoints. Current Go schedules client does not expose these update methods, so this is a TS parity gap.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

remaining_limitations: Pinned-engine legacy workflow and tenant queue metrics handlers are deprecated; their old SDK methods explicitly return UnsupportedOperation. Supported task metrics, task queues and task stats use current endpoints.

Prometheus text decoding is protocol-tested; the local live engine verifies the disabled-configuration error. A production Prometheus federation server and tenant entitlement are not configured in these tests.
items.original_gap: Rust exposes reduced workflow/queue counts and hardcodes live cancelled_runs to zero. Missing Go task-queue metrics and richer query parameters; TS additionally exposes status aggregation, task stats and Prometheus scraping.
items.acceptance: Implemented contract and evidence are maintained in the feature support matrix.

items.original_gap: No native OTel spans/context propagation or public middleware pipeline. User-written handler wrappers are possible but not equivalent built-in SDK support.
items.acceptance: Implement the stated operational contract and supply matching local/protocol/live evidence.
remaining_limitations: Native tracing requires the default-enabled opentelemetry feature and an application-managed 0.32 provider/exporter. Hatchet collector auth, deterministic engine reparenting and automatic propagation of Hatchet attributes onto every application span are not configured by this SDK.

items.original_gap: No workflow/task idempotency key expression, TTL/status-based policy or collision-result handling. Error::DedupeViolation alone does not implement this behavior.
items.acceptance: Implement the stated operational contract and supply matching local/protocol/live evidence.
remaining_limitations: The conservative verified SDK support floor is v0.111.0. In-memory idempotency is explicitly unsupported; policy belongs to workflow registration, including one-task workflows.

items.original_gap: List/upsert exist, but there is no pause-until API for holding queued runs behind a rate-limit key.
items.acceptance: Implement the stated operational contract and supply matching local/protocol/live evidence.
remaining_limitations: The verified SDK support floor is v0.114.0.

items.original_gap: Workflow sticky policy is rendered and durable child request uses opts.sticky as desired_worker_id. Normal gRPC run dispatch does not consume opts.sticky and explicitly sends desired_worker_id=None.
items.acceptance: Implement the stated operational contract and supply matching local/protocol/live evidence.
remaining_limitations: Eventual restart recovery verified for current worker IDs on baseline/current in~61–63 seconds; old45-second failures reflect an insufficient deadline in those scenarios. TS submissions to the same Rust workers recovered similarly; full official-worker isolation and exact internal cause remain unproven. No low-latency restart SLA or stale-worker-ID remapping is claimed.

items.original_gap: There is no CI-enforced mapping from official SDK operations to real-engine behavior tests. Twelve live tests cover core cases; durable eviction/restore/branch, engine restart recovery, large fanout, broad management APIs and full scheduling/concurrency/condition semantics do not have equivalent live coverage. This does not classify implemented but untested primitives as absent.
items.acceptance: Implement the stated operational contract and supply matching local/protocol/live evidence.
remaining_limitations: Pinned baseline/current engine CI definitions are supplied and their suites pass locally. Remote GitHub Actions execution awaits pushing this commit.
The official TS/Go SDK suites are not executed. This proof does not exhaustively compare all scheduling semantics or cover worker-process crashes; those limitations remain partial in the matrix.

items.acceptance: Preview server coalescing, exact member results, broadcast, failure and cancellation supported on verified engine v0.114.0. Worker and workflow configurations must match; durable and local-engine simulation unsupported. See batch-tasks.md and feature-support.md.
items.original_gap: No batch handler/configuration for size/time-based server coalescing and per-member results. Existing run_many/bulk triggering is a distinct capability. Upstream marks batch tasks preview/beta.

items.acceptance: Typed per-failure retry delay on normal/durable and batch failure events; verified normal/durable scheduling and retry limits on v0.111.0/v0.114.0. Bounded version check falls back explicitly to static policy for older/unknown engines. See retry-after.md.
items.original_gap: No RetryAfterError equivalent or completion-event retry-after encoding. Static retry counts and backoff exist. Go gates this feature at engine v0.111.0, above Rust v0.94.14.

items.acceptance: Current TS preview durable topics implemented with exact cursors/reset/metadata, serialized producer sequences, batching/older-RPC fallback, upload/fetch and reconnect/cancellation. Verified on v0.114.0 with required entitlement; legacy fallback/retention errors protocol-tested. See durable-topics.md.
items.original_gap: No streams feature client for publish, resumable cursor-based events, reset and topic metadata. This is distinct from workflow event streaming and is currently a preview feature. Not counted as a Go feature-client gap.

items.acceptance: Explicit real official-sidecar engine/client lifecycle with bundled persistent Postgres, verified content-addressed binary cache, private handshake and owned cleanup. Real cold/post-fix/offline-warm native proofs; API-less raw mode works, full Rust client needs REST. See embedded.md.
items.original_gap: Rust has InMemoryTransport and Docker smoke scripts, but no supported API for booting an embedded real engine with persistence.

items.acceptance: Reusable offline JSON Schema validation and Serde-deserialization schema generation, normal/durable/member enforcement before handlers, invalid configuration before mutation/start, exact workflow metadata and non-retryable typed decode errors. See input-schemas.md.
remaining_limitations: Offline self-contained schemas only; arbitrary Zod callbacks/coercion/transforms are language-specific. Custom Serde adapters may need Schemars annotations; no exhaustive official SDK or JSON Schema conformance suite is claimed.

items.acceptance: Distinct /livez always200 while responsive and /readyz connection-dependent200/503; preserves legacy Rust /health JSON/status. Bounded HTTP handling, HEAD/routes and owned cleanup. Actual restart readiness transition and liveness verified on baseline/current. See health-probes.md.
